# Stallledger

Stallledger is an inventory tracker for small farmers'-market vendors — the person
who sells jam, eggs, or seedlings from a single stall on Saturday mornings and keeps
their stock counts in a notebook the rest of the week.

## Audience

Sole-proprietor market vendors. They are not technical, they work from a phone or a
cheap laptop, and they have at most a few dozen product lines. They care about two
questions: "what do I still have?" and "what sold last weekend?"

## Key screens

### Inventory

The Inventory screen lists every product the vendor stocks — name, unit (jar, dozen,
bunch), quantity on hand, and price per unit. Vendors adjust counts here after a
market day and flag items that are running low so they know what to restock or
re-make before the next market.

### Vendors

The Vendors screen holds the vendor's own stall profile and the neighboring stalls
they trade with — stall name, market days, and what each stall carries. It exists so
a vendor can quickly answer "who at this market sells honey?" when a customer asks.
